title: requirements before start
name: Requirements before start
rule: Before a long form, communicate requirements up front (time, materials, deadlines, attempt limits, whether progress is saved).

citation.source: NN/g — 4 Principles to Reduce Cognitive Load in Forms

pass_when: Before the first field of a long form, time, materials, deadlines, attempt limits, and save behavior that apply are stated.
fail_when: Those requirements appear only mid-form or after failure — or not at all on a long form.
overview: State time, materials, deadlines, attempt limits, and save behavior before a long form.
apply_when: Starting long forms that impose time, materials, or attempt constraints.
not_when: Short forms with no special requirements to announce up front.
agent_hint: Announce applicable time, materials, deadlines, limits, and save behavior first.
description: Before a long form, communicate requirements up front — time, materials, deadlines, attempt limits, whether progress is saved. Pass when those that apply are stated before the first field; fail when they appear only mid-form or after failure, or not at all on a long form. Up-front requirements prevent mid-flow surprises that waste the user’s effort.
